### Review skipped — opt-out keyword in branch name 🛑

The source branch `feature/noergloff-thing` contains the opt-out keyword `noergloff`, so the auto-review was
skipped. No LLM or Jira calls were made for this PR.

**What to do**
- Rename the branch to remove the keyword and push again; the next webhook event will trigger a full review.
- Or @mention the bot explicitly in a comment if you want a one-off review on this branch; mentions are not
  muted.

**Configure**
- The keyword is set via `REVIEW_OPT_OUT_BRANCH_KEYWORD` on the noergler service (empty string disables the
  feature).
agents_missing:
### Review skipped — no `AGENTS.md` found 🛑

This repository has no `AGENTS.md` on the PR branch or the target branch, so the review was not run.

**What to do**
- Add `AGENTS.md` to the repository root with what the code does not show: invariants that must never break,
  your team's conventions, decisions and their why, traps you have learned from. That is what the review holds
  your code to; without it, it sees only the diff.
- A few lines are enough to start. Mark rules that should block a merge with `[blocking]`. In a monorepo,
  `AGENTS.md` in a subdirectory adds rules for that part.
- No project rules wanted? An empty `AGENTS.md` is enough; the review then runs on general rules.
- Push the file; the next webhook event on this PR triggers a full review.

**On the ETH study**
The often-quoted [ETH study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988) does not advise against it: files written by
people should, per its authors, hold what code and README do not show, such as conventions and non-functional
requirements. What did not help were files generated by agents.
diff_too_large:
### Review skipped — diff too large 🛑

The PR diff exceeds 10 MiB, more than fits in one review even after compression, so the review was not run.

**What to do**
- Split the change into smaller PRs, or move generated files, vendored code and lockfile churn into their own
  PR.
- Push the smaller change and the next webhook event on this PR will trigger a full review.
agents_too_large_nolink:
### Review skipped — `AGENTS.md` too large 🛑

`AGENTS.md` weighs in at ~12'345 tokens, exceeding the configured hard limit of 7'000 tokens. Oversized agent
instructions crowd out the actual diff, degrade review quality (context rot), and inflate inference cost, so
the review was not run. The [ETH study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988) says the same: context files
*"should only contain specific additional instructions beyond what is already available in the codebase"*.

**What to do**
- Keep what the code does not show: invariants, conventions, decisions and their why. Cut what the code or the
  README already says; replace prose with terse rules.
- Move detailed reference material into separate files and link to them; keep the main file lean.
- Push the slimmer file and the next webhook event on this PR will trigger a full review.

**Configure**
- Raise the limit via `REVIEW_AGENTS_MD_MAX_TOKENS` on the noergler service, or set it to `0` to disable the
  hard cut-off entirely (the soft warning via `REVIEW_AGENTS_MD_WARN_TOKENS` remains).

**Further reading**
- [Upsun — The research is in: your AGENTS.md is probably too long (2026-02-23)](https://developer.upsun.com/posts/ai/agents-md-less-is-more)
- [Augment Code — A good AGENTS.md is a model upgrade. A bad one is worse than no docs at all (2026-04-22)](https://www.augmentcode.com/blog/how-to-write-good-agents-dot-md-files)
- [Caveman — Claude Code skill, "why use many token when few token do trick"](https://github.com/juliusbrussee/caveman)
